text:
When Ottawa traded its captain to Florida in June, the easy story was that the Senators had lost their identity. Five months later they lead the Atlantic, have points in nine straight (7-0-2), and are taking 59% of the expected goals in that run (the quality of chances each side gets). They already beat Brady Tkachuk once, 5-1 in Ottawa on Oct. 21, even after he scored the first goal. One reporter's post put the turnaround on Travis Green, and it's hard to argue with how this team defends.

The other half of it is Linus Ullmark. After a season that cost Ottawa 13.3 goals against expected, he is +12.1 this year with a .941 save rate, and 5-0-0 with a .935 over his last five starts. That's a heater, and heaters end, but for now he's the best story in the division. Tim Stützle drives the offense, now beside Dylan Cozens and Jesper Zetterlund with William Eklund out until January. Nick Cousins is back in the lineup after the Jakob Chychrun hit that had everyone talking.

Florida's story is who walks in the door. Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand have both been skating, and reports call them possible to return tonight. Without them the Panthers have leaned on the Tkachuks: Matthew leads the team with 32 points and has been playing beside Sam Reinhart and his brother, while Lars Eller's minutes have jumped from about 12 to 17. Sam Bennett has a hat trick in his last game and 10 points in 10, though our numbers say that run is mostly bounces. The Panthers are 3-1-1 in their last five but lost the chance battle in those games (46%).

Discipline is the matchup to watch. Florida takes 5.1 penalties a game and has a power play worth 1.05 expected goals a night, against an Ottawa penalty kill allowing 0.78. Jacob Markstrom (+2.1) starts for Florida. Ottawa is 94% to make the playoffs by our count; Florida is 63%, and six points back.
headline: Brady Tkachuk gets his second look at Ottawa
